# Separation loses exactly the relation

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`separation-loses-the-relation` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](separation-loses-the-relation.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Describing the parts separately gives back the whole exactly where it is rectangular; a relation forms only by joint action, lasts under separate laws that merge nothing that occurs, and ends only by loss or joint action; parity is a whole its pairs do not give back.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. For a whole on A × B, the combinations that occur, it is rectangular where whatever goes with one part goes with every other: (a, b) and (a′, b′) occurring give (a, b′). Its separated description admits a pair where each part occurs with something. Separation keeps every combination that occurs, and admits only what occurs exactly where the whole is rectangular. (`Becoming.Rectangular`, `Becoming.Separated`, `Becoming.separated_of_whole`, `Becoming.separation_faithful_iff`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
2. Two parts that always go alike, described separately, can go apart: for the whole on Bool × Bool where the parts are equal, the separated description admits (true, false), which does not occur. (`Becoming.separation_admits_extra`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
3. A relation held by the whole and by no pair: in the even-parity triples on Bool, any two values of any two places complete to an even triple, and (true, false, false) is not one. (`Becoming.flipIf`, `Becoming.EvenThree`, `Becoming.whole_not_in_pairs`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
4. On Specker's three boxes read through their three pairs, every reading of the boxes is allowed by every pair under even parity, and the pairs do not give the whole back: not every reading the pairs allow is of even parity. (`Becoming.evenBoxes`, `Becoming.evenBoxes_glued`, `Becoming.evenBoxes_not_determined`, `Becoming.restrict`, `Becoming.Glued`, `Becoming.PartsDetermine`, `Becoming.Specker.Box`, `Becoming.Specker.within`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
5. A law's image of a whole is the configurations it leads to from the whole. A law moving each part by itself, (a, b) to (f a, g b) for any f and g, keeps a rectangular whole rectangular. The law copying the first part into the second leads from the full whole on Bool × Bool to the parts being equal, which is not rectangular. (`Becoming.imageOf`, `Becoming.Rectangular.image_of_separate`, `Becoming.copy_relates`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
6. Where f merges no two first parts that occur in the whole and g no two second parts, a rectangular image under the law moving each part by itself comes only from a rectangular whole, so a whole that is not rectangular stays so under that law. (`Becoming.Rectangular.of_image_injective`, `Becoming.relation_persists`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
7. A law sending the first part to one value, however it moves the second, leads from any whole to a rectangular one. (`Becoming.forgetting_unrelates`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
8. The coupling taking (x, y) to (x, y turned over where x holds) on Bool × Bool undoes itself; it leads from “the second part is false”, which is rectangular, to a whole that is not rectangular, and acting again leads back to “the second part is false”. (`Becoming.couple`, `Becoming.couple_couple`, `Becoming.coupling_relates_and_unrelates`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
9. Along the courses of n moves of a determined law's process from a whole: under a law moving each part by itself, a rectangular whole reaches only rectangular wholes at every n; where f and g merge nothing at all, a whole that is not rectangular reaches only wholes that are not rectangular at every n. (`Becoming.Courses.reachedFrom`, `Becoming.Courses.courses_keep_unrelated`, `Becoming.Courses.relation_persists_courses`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
10. Along such courses, one move of copying the first part into the second leads from every configuration of Bool × Bool to the parts being equal, not rectangular; after one move of a law sending the first part to one value, every course leads to a rectangular whole; one move of the coupling from “the second part is false” leads to a whole that is not rectangular, and two moves lead back. (`Becoming.Courses.copy_relates_course`, `Becoming.Courses.forgetting_unrelates_courses`, `Becoming.Courses.coupling_course`)
    - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No premise: separation_faithful_iff is two-way and holds for every whole; Rectangular.image_of_separate holds for any f and g.
- relation_persists needs f and g to merge nothing that occurs, and relation_persists_courses to merge nothing at all (local conditions, written into the theorems).
- For the witnesses: parity, copying and couple are on Bool.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Relation is stated for wholes of two parts, by rectangularity, the standard product criterion; three parts enter only through the parity witness.
- The laws do not characterize which joint laws keep wholes rectangular.
- That a joint law merging nothing can end a relation rests on one witness, the coupling on Bool × Bool. Witness: `Becoming.coupling_relates_and_unrelates`.
- Parts giving back a whole across contexts and the separation of two parts are not stated as instance and law of each other, the two parts having different types.
- **Counterexample:** A whole that is not rectangular gains combinations when described separately (separation_admits_extra); the even parity of three parts is held by no pair (whole_not_in_pairs); a lossless coupling can end a relation (coupling_relates_and_unrelates), so losing nothing does not keep a relation without “moving each part by itself”. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Description.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps.

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Following Ren's “push the frontier, as far as possible” of 12 October 2026, answering Ren's “the framing may lose something” and “what makes a pair, a pair?”: what describing the parts separately deducts is exactly the relation; “what can go together” is the record at a moment of “how they go on”. Readings (an AI reading): a correlation is the memory of a meeting; 三生万物 read as three being the least number at which a whole holds a relation no part holds. The other way parts fail a whole (parts allowing what no whole has) is no_whole of claims-shown-in-context, on the same three pairs.

<a id="dependencies--依赖"></a>
### Dependencies

- **formal-reuse**: [claims-shown-in-context](claims-shown-in-context.md). Reuses restrict, Glued, PartsDetermine and Specker's boxes and pairs: on the same three pairs parity is a whole its pairs do not give back.
  - Output: What a whole allows within a context, what the parts glue to, whether the parts give the whole back; three boxes and three pairs.
  - Input: Parity as the witness of the first way parts fail a whole.
  - Preserved conditions: None. [Context.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Context.lean)
- related, not a proved adapter: [the-split-that-makes-sense](the-split-that-makes-sense.md). Same module: the split that makes sense, relative to the map; here, what any description cutting a whole into parts loses.
- related, not a proved adapter: [projection-carrying-a-law](projection-carrying-a-law.md). A projection carries a law exactly where what it lumps goes alike; here laws moving each part by itself keep wholes rectangular, and joint laws can relate or unrelate the parts.
- related, not a proved adapter: [gluing-under-parity](gluing-under-parity.md). The exact law for the same kind of case of parts failing a whole: for parity constraints, context-free readings exist exactly where no selection of contexts contradicts.
